content:
If you are a large-scale app user who has been using the Apple Watch beta this summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps cannot launch on watchOS 27. Apple has identified this issue and is automatically updating apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

This update is being pushed via the App Store, and the update notes read: "This app has been updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features are included."

Apple has notified developers this week that the related processing will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27 (along with iOS 27 and other new operating systems) is expected to be released to the public around mid-September, so the update has been rolled out early.

Apple stated that due to issues with the arm64 encoding of some watchOS apps, this processing is necessary. It appears they are automatically reprocessing and repackaging apps to fix binary compatibility issues so that existing apps can continue to run, and developers do not need to take any action.
